name: Appointed counsel in state felony trials
description: A U.S. Supreme Court decision required state courts to provide counsel to felony defendants unable to afford a lawyer.

impact.note: Extended to all state felony trials in one country a right to counsel already held in federal courts and many states; a few later rulings widened it.

date.label: 18 March 1963
date.basis: Date of the Supreme Court decision.

events.statement: The Supreme Court reversed Gideon’s Florida conviction and held that an indigent criminal defendant has a right to counsel in the case before it.
events.scope: This documented community and episode; not a universal first.

evidence.supports: The 18 March 1963 opinion overruled Betts and applied the right to counsel to a state felony case.

contributions.resource: Petitioned after counsel was denied in his Florida felony case.

evidence.supports: The 18 March 1963 opinion overruled Betts and applied the right to counsel to a state felony case.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence gathered for this scoped capability, not global priority.

caveats: The ruling was a legal guarantee in U.S. state criminal proceedings; earlier defense systems existed and effective access, eligibility in other cases and quality require separate evidence.

research.note: Initial source pass; independent review is outstanding. Independent review checked the decision and procedural scope against the Court’s opinion; the formal guarantee does not establish effective delivery.
